headline: Approved bonds for Nashua Public Library renovation design, Pine Hill fire station replacement design, and $9 million ERP system replacement.
summary: Approved bond authorizations for a fire training facility, Pine Hill fire station work, fire station repairs, the Nashua Public Library, a Four Hills Landfill project, and an enterprise resource planning system. Approved the Juliana Avenue street acceptance and an amended ordinance allowing electronic public comment for people with disabilities. Referred new resolutions and ordinances on garage leases and parking permits to committees.
decisions: Referred the John Flatley Company request to purchase City-owned parcels to the Committee on Infrastructure.
Placed the Mayor's veto communication on Ordinance O-26-002 and the Public Works letter on file.
Granted final passage of the Juliana Avenue street acceptance petition; motion carried.
Referred the appointment of Dalia Ragas as Deputy Treasurer/Deputy Tax Collector to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee.
Referred the Mayor's appointments of Cathy Prevost, Lisa Tourangeau, and Jennifer Bishop to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee.
Adopted R-26-064, Amended, authorizing bonds not to exceed $5,173,428 for capital equipment, by roll call vote of 13 yea and 1 nay.
Adopted R-26-067, authorizing bonds not to exceed $3,000,000 for design and ancillary costs to renovate the Nashua Public Library, by roll call vote of 10 yea and 4 nay.
Adopted R-26-068, authorizing bonds not to exceed $1,500,000 for a fire training facility, by roll call vote of 13 yea and 1 nay.
Adopted R-26-069, authorizing bonds not to exceed $1,000,000 for design and ancillary costs to replace the Pine Hill fire station, by roll call vote of 13 yea and 1 nay.
Adopted R-26-070, authorizing bonds not to exceed $1,000,000 for deferred capital maintenance of fire stations, by roll call vote of 13 yea and 1 nay.
Adopted R-26-071, authorizing bonds not to exceed $9,000,000 for replacement and modernization of the city-wide ERP system, by roll call vote of 10 yea and 4 nay.
Adopted R-26-075, authorizing the Mayor to enter a second amended federal aid project agreement for the Taylor Falls and Veterans Bridges and to accept an additional $231,941.29.
Adopted R-26-076, accepting $45,180 from the U.S. Department of Justice for police grant activity.
Adopted Ordinance O-26-024, authorizing additional stop signs to make an all way stop at French Street and Abbott Street.
Withdrew the motion to amend O-26-002 to add all committees.
Withdrew the motion to reverse the August 9, 2022 decision that ends access to Zoom meetings.
Approved replacing Ordinance O-26-002 with the amended document placed on members' desks, by roll call vote of 12 yea and 2 nay.
Adopted Ordinance O-26-002, as amended, allowing electronic public comment for people with disabilities, by roll call vote of 11 yea and 3 nay.
Adopted R-26-062, authorizing bonds not to exceed $2,000,000 for various improvements at the Four Hills Landfill, by roll call vote of 11 yea and 3 nay.
Referred R-26-077, a supplemental appropriation of $146,617.94 into the Opioid Abatement Expendable Trust Fund, to the Budget Review Committee and set a public hearing for November 23, 2026.
Referred R-26-078, authorizing a first amendment to the High Street Garage lease with Nashua Apartment Ventures, LLC, to the Finance Committee.
Referred R-26-079, authorizing a School Street Parking Garage lease with Nashua Apartment Ventures, LLC, to the Finance Committee.
Referred O-26-027, amending parking permits for the High Street Garage, to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee.
Referred O-26-028, amending parking permits for the School Street Parking Garage, to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee.

A:2 II. 
  
President Lori Wilshire presided; City Clerk Dan Healey recorded. 
 
Prayer was offered by City Clerk Dan Healey; Alderman Derek Thibeault led in the Pledge to the Flag.
